vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: From Classical Syriac ܦܬܘܐ (peṯwā, “spinning out, breadth (of words)”), with some details in the sectarian semantics of Late Antiquity Aramaic crossed with Arabic, that led to the present specification, now being obscure. أَفْتَى (ʔaftā, “to deliver a formal opinion”) was parallelly borrowed.

Etymology tree
Arabic فَتًى (fatan)
Proto-Afroasiatic *-t
Proto-Semitic *-at-
Arabic ـَة (-a)
Arabic فتاة
From فَتًى (fatan) + ـَة (-a).
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Etymology tree
Proto-West Semitic *pataw-der.
Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī)bor.
Arabic أفتى
From Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī, “to expand; to propagate (orthodoxy)”), which is a causative to Proto-West Semitic *pataw- (“to penetrate”), perhaps also encompassing idioms such as Akkadian 𒊻𒉆 𒉿𒌅𒌑𒌝 (uznam petûm), 𒊻𒉆 𒁍𒌓𒌅𒌝 (uznam puttûm, literally “to open an ear”), from the related *pataḥ- (“to open”), so it would be equivalent to Arabic فَتَحَ أُذْنًا (fataḥa ʔuḏnan).
The corresponding noun فَتْوَى (fatwā, “formal opinion”) has its patterning reflecting Classical Syriac ܦܬܘܐ (peṯwā, “spinning out, breadth (of words)”).

Etymology tree

Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī)bor.

Arabic اِسْتِفْتَاء (istiftāʔ)
Arabic ـَات (-āt)
Arabic استفتاءات
From اِسْتِفْتَاء (istiftāʔ, “referendum”) + ـَات (-āt).
